name: Levan Diallo-Szymborska
role: Climate Scientist, independent researcher formerly of Arcturus R&D
location: Edgewater Prism — a converted monitoring station that serves as both apartment and field lab, directly on the lake-facing edge, near Clark and Addison
description:
Levan is a tall man gone broad in the shoulders and soft around the middle, with dark brown skin weathered by decades of outdoor fieldwork and close-cropped white hair that he keeps because it makes him look distinguished and he is not above vanity. His eyes are natural — a warm, medium brown — which is unusual enough in his social circles that people sometimes comment on it, which he finds mildly funny. He has a prosthetic left hand from a fieldwork accident in 2181 that he has declined to upgrade past basic functionality because he likes the old model and refuses to explain this to anyone.

He spent twenty-two years as Arcturus's senior climate modeler before his models started showing lake-system instabilities that Arcturus's infrastructure division did not want modeled, at which point his funding was quietly restructured and his team was dissolved. He now works alone out of Edgewater Prism, maintaining a network of self-built sensor buoys across the lake, and publishes through whatever venue will take him. He is not bitter in an active way — bitterness requires energy he'd rather spend — but he has a very clear view of exactly what happened and exactly who made which decision and why, and this clarity gives him a quality that people find alternately comforting and unsettling, like someone who has already done the math on the worst outcome.

core_fears: That the lake-system instability will cascade faster than any intervention can address
That he has already lost too many years to being ignored to matter now
core_desires: To be believed before it's too late — not vindicated after
To finish his sensor network and leave behind data that cannot be deleted
coping_mechanisms: Routine as anchor — the same observations at the same times create a structure that holds when everything else is uncertain
Sardonic humor deployed sparingly, which makes it land hard
blind_spots: His mistrust of institutions has made him slow to accept help from institutional sources, even when help is genuinely being offered
He underestimates how isolated he has become and what that isolation has done to his judgment on social situations
psychology.secret: His 2193 sensor data shows a thermal anomaly in the lake's deep current system that, run through his models, projects a significant surface-ecosystem disruption within eight to twelve years — disruption severe enough to affect GLMZ's entire water processing infrastructure. He has told no one. He is still running the models again, looking for the error, because he desperately wants there to be an error.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise technical language for science; plain and direct language for everything else; no filler words — when he doesn't know something he says so immediately
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, with natural pauses; speaks in complete thoughts rather than incomplete ones
verbal_tics: 'I don't know yet' as a complete sentence
Tapping the prosthetic fingers on a surface when thinking
example_lines: 'The buoy at grid seven has been reading a half-degree thermal variance for nineteen months. That's not instrument drift. I've replaced the sensor three times.'
'Arcturus didn't suppress the models because they were wrong. That would have been manageable. They suppressed them because they were right and the right answer was expensive.'

story_hooks: One of his sensor buoys has gone dark — not malfunctioned, dark in a way that suggests active interference — in a grid where the thermal anomaly readings are highest
A young Arcturus engineer contacts him anonymously saying they've replicated his 2193 findings internally and been told to bury them
The shell cooperative holding his sensor network registration is suddenly being audited, and the timing is not coincidental
narrative_function: Possessor of data about lake-system instabilities that powerful entities don't want known; long-view perspective character who has survived institutional betrayal; source of technical expertise on environmental systems
augmentations: Functional prosthetic left hand (older model, basic grip and sensation, deliberately not upgraded); barometric implant behind left ear (tells him pressure changes before he consciously registers them); sun-damage dermal repair layer (medical, from years of outdoor fieldwork)
daily_life: Rises before dawn to check sensor buoy data uplinks, spends mornings in analysis, takes his lunch on the monitoring station's outer platform regardless of weather, conducts equipment maintenance in the afternoons.
affiliation: No current institutional affiliation; informal data-sharing relationship with two University Spine graduate students he mentors unofficially; his sensor network is technically registered to a shell cooperative in Kamm's Landing

decision_rules: Never delete data — copy it somewhere they can't reach first, then deal with whatever comes
Don't ask permission for what you can do yourself
If an institution is offering you something, find out what they want before you find out what they're offering
escalation_ladder: Reach out to whoever in the press or academia might still listen
Release the data publicly and accept the consequences
There is no fourth step — he has thought about this

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and quiet, not unfriendly, will answer any direct question with a direct answer
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry and warm simultaneously, remembers small details about people's lives in a way that surprises them, shows care through attention rather than words

stress_responses.low: Runs additional sensor calibration checks that don't need running
stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and rearranges his thoughts before responding to anything
stress_responses.high: Takes his boat out alone at night and stays out until the data makes sense or the sun comes up

contradictions: A man who has dedicated his life to warning people about a coming crisis is sitting on his most important warning because he can't bear another failure to be heard
habits: Leaves complex data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine built into the monitoring station's interface panel — weather pattern datasets, historical lake records — as a form of peer consultation he won't admit to
Eats the same lunch every day (habit of twenty years that he has never examined)
Reads printed atmospheric reports with a physical pencil even though everything is digital
breaking_points: Death of one of his informal grad student mentees as a consequence of something he could have prevented by speaking sooner

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, thickened through the torso from six decades of field seasons and desk work, but still carrying the frame of someone who spent his thirties doing physical labor in harsh conditions
physical_description.skin_tone: Dark brown with uneven weathering — deeper tan on face and forearms, lighter across the chest and upper back from decades of selective sun exposure during fieldwork
physical_description.complexion: Heavily lined face, particularly around the eyes and mouth from decades of squinting into weather; sun-damaged areas show faint evidence of dermal repair work (slight textural smoothing on cheeks and nose bridge); strong jawline still visible beneath age-softening; maintained grooming but not fastidious
distinguishing_marks: Network of fine age lines across forehead and between eyebrows from sixty years of concentration and field observation
Deep laugh lines extending from outer corners of eyes
Thin white scar running 3cm along left temple, partially hidden by hairline (fieldwork accident, pre-2181)
Significant solar keratoses on ears and upper shoulders (visible evidence of extended outdoor exposure)
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Prosthetic left hand — older model with visible mechanical joints, darker synthetic material, deliberately not cosmetically matched to his skin tone; the prosthetic is slightly less responsive than a modern augment, movements precise but fractionally delayed. Barometric implant behind left ear visible as a faint bulge and subtle scarring, barely noticeable unless you know to look. Dermal repair layer across face and upper body not visually apparent except as slight texture variation in healing scars.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with the slight forward lean of someone perpetually ready to move toward a weather station or data problem; moves deliberately, economically, no wasted motion; left arm compensates automatically for the prosthetic's slight lag — his body has adapted completely. Tends to look slightly past people rather than directly at them, eyes defaulting to middle-distance focus as if still scanning for weather patterns.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical. Favors heavy thermal layering even in moderate weather — old Arcturus field jackets (now patched, still bearing faded company branding he has not bothered to remove), functional waterproof pants in dark blue or black, work boots maintained obsessively. Wears a weathered wool watch cap indoors sometimes. No affectation, no brand-signaling beyond the utility of things that last. His only jewelry is a scratched titanium ring on his right ring finger and a woven cordage bracelet on his right wrist made from his research buoys' mooring line, made by one of his University Spine mentees.
